page.title: GameForgeJS — Your game. Your code. JavaScript.
hero.intro: From your first character to worlds of your own. A framework for browser games, with classes, components and control over what you build.
hero.node: Node.js is an optional development tool.
demos.title: Code comes to life.
demos.description: Playable examples of movement, combat, cameras, rendering and game rules. The demos are experimental.
demos.platformer: Combos, hitboxes, inventory, skills and manifest-authored levels.
demos.sky: Four expeditions, a gamepad-ready 3D menu, checkpoints and moving platforms.
demos.toon: Animated characters, five sentries, three areas and rippling shallow water.
demos.note: The demos are small experimental games. Complete courses and upcoming goals are described below.
architecture.title: The framework handles
architecture.description: Levels organize scenes. Entities receive behaviors. Screens and renderers handle presentation. Evolve your game with the classes you already use.
architecture.example: A modular runtime example. The template configures the import map and provides the first level.
progress.intro: Modules organize distribution and extensions. The primary path remains
progress.select: Select runtime groups and addons in
progress.dependencies: . The build includes group dependencies while preserving your game structure.
progress.addons: Parallax, state machines and platformer movement extracted from the demos. Classes built on the framework services and its existing engine.
progress.complete: From zero to a complete game.
progress.goal: Checkpoints already cover action combat, animated models and shallow water. The goal remains a complete Toon adventure and a 2D platformer with at least 20 levels and varied enemy behaviors.
progress.course: Zero to Hero is still in progress. Games, code, assets, lessons and validation will be completed together.
start.intro: Start with a template, choose the modules you need and build your game step by step. The demos above use that same runtime.
start.server: at the address printed by the server.
footer.description: A framework in progress. Built to learn, experiment and create.
footer.author: Created by Patrick Faustino Camello.
